cards.q: What is PIM-SM and why is it the production default?
cards.a: PIM-SM (Sparse Mode) is the production default for IP multicast. It assumes receivers are sparse and uses a pull model: nobody receives traffic until they explicitly join, and joins flow through a Rendezvous Point (RP) that builds a shared (*,G) tree, which may later switch to a source-based (S,G) SPT.

cards.q: Walk through the PIM-SM pull model sequence.
cards.a: A receiver sends an IGMP report; the DR joins (*,G) toward the RP so a shared tree is built; the source registers to the RP; then the last-hop router performs the SPT switchover. Traffic flows only to those who asked.

cards.q: What are the roles of the RP, DR, FHR, and LHR in PIM-SM?
cards.a: The RP is the core of the shared tree where sources register and receivers join; the DR is the first-hop router for the source or last-hop for the receiver; the FHR is the source's DR and the LHR is the receiver's DR.

cards.q: What are the two PIM-SM tree types?
cards.a: The shared tree (*,G) via the RP is used initially, and the shortest-path tree (S,G) goes directly from the source after the SPT switchover.

cards.q: How does a source register with the RP?
cards.a: The source sends multicast to the FHR, which sends a register message that encapsulates the multicast packet in unicast to the RP; the RP answers with a register-stop and then forwards traffic down the shared tree.

cards.q: What does ip pim spt-threshold 0 do, and what is the default?
cards.a: It makes the last-hop router switch immediately to the (S,G) shortest-path tree; the default is 0 kbps, so switchover is immediate by default and yields the shortest path with best latency.

cards.q: Which commands enable PIM-SM with a static RP?
cards.a: Globally ip multicast-routing and ip pim rp-address <RP-IP>; per interface use ip pim sparse-mode.

cards.q: How can the static RP mapping be replaced?
cards.a: Auto-RP or BSR provide dynamic group-to-RP mapping, removing the need for a static ip pim rp-address.
show ip mroute, show ip pim rp mapping, show ip pim interface, and show ip pim neighbor; debug ip pim for diagnosis.

cards.q: No multicast traffic and registering is failing in PIM-SM; where do you look?
cards.a: Check the RP mapping and reachability with show ip pim rp mapping and ping the RP, and use debug ip pim to trace FHR-to-RP register failures.

cards.q: Traffic stays on the shared tree only and never switches to the SPT; why?
cards.a: The spt-threshold is preventing (S,G) switchover; check show ip mroute and the ip pim spt-threshold setting.

cards.q: PIM-SM shows an RP mismatch between static and dynamic mapping; what do you verify?
cards.a: That the group-to-RP mapping is consistent; verify with show ip pim rp mapping.

cards.q: Can PIM-SM operate without an RP?
cards.a: No. PIM-SM requires an RP for the shared tree and the register process; without it the multicast tree cannot be built.

cards.q: What is the quick review summary for PIM-SM?
cards.a: Pull/join model, an RP is required, shared tree (*,G) then SPT (S,G), register is unicast to the RP, threshold 0 means immediate switchover, it is the default mode, and config is rp-address plus ip pim sparse-mode.
